findings.issue: SM-04 table gaps. The spec needs transitions that are not in A03's 16-transition SM-04 table (live->suspended and suspended->live only), yet it says the node 'adds no state' and must refuse every unlisted pair with SM04_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION. (a) Pause from soft_cap_reached is not in the table, and resume always goes to live, so the soft-cap flag is lost. (b) A suspended offer has no exit at closes_at: 'closes_at keeps running', but there is no suspended->closed, so it is stuck forever. (c) The A48 kill switch, a G10 halt and an A33 tenant suspension all 'pause every offering through pause', but approved, scheduled, draft and compliance_review have no pause transition. The builder must either break the frozen table or leave these cases unhandled, and the exhaustive-pair oracle fails either way.
findings.fix: Decide and write down the behaviour, then reopen A03 as a spec defect if the table has to change. Option 1: add soft_cap_reached->suspended (resume goes back to the stored paused_from state), add suspended->closed at closes_at, and add a publication hold on approved/scheduled (a flag that blocks scheduled->live, not a new state). Option 2: state that pause is refused in soft_cap_reached and that the close sweep resumes and then closes a suspended offer. List the resulting from/to pairs in oracle item (b) and in the State coverage pass criterion.

findings.issue: Ownership of close, fail and refund overlaps with A38, and A36's field names do not match what A37 reads. A38 says it drives live|soft_cap_reached->closed (on closes_at, on hard_cap_reached at exactly 100 percent, and on a close_early approval), closed->failed (R1) and failed->refunding (R3), all 'through A36'. A36 instead defines its own schedule_sweep close, its own pro-rata close at 120 percent, and its own close_early, cancel_and_refund and revert_and_refund effectors. Its internal transition endpoint accepts only A37, the unnamed finalise-and-mint node (mint.reconciled) and A48, so A38's calls would get 403. A37 reads Offering fields A36 never defines: total_units, hard_cap_units, holder_cap_bps, fee_bps, allow_oversubscription, cancellable_until_close, fund_at, cooling_off_days, rule_pack_id. A36 uses supply_units, per_investor_cap_bps, transaction_fee_bps, oversubscription_cap_bps and rule_pack_code instead.
findings.fix: Give each trigger one owner. Suggested split: A36 decides when a close is due; A38 performs close, fail, finalising and refunding by calling A36's exported transition functions. Add A38 and those transition kinds to the internal endpoint's allow-list. Remove A36's duplicate close_early, cancel_and_refund and revert_and_refund effectors, or map each one onto A38's action codes. Make the pro-rata ceiling agree with A38's hard_cap_reached. Export an OfferingTerms type from index.ts using the exact field names A37 reads, including hard_cap_units, allow_oversubscription (true when oversubscription_cap_bps > 0), cancellable_until_close with its default, and fee_bps. Add a contract test that A37's import compiles.

findings.issue: The go-live sequence contradicts journey J12, and the custody binding is circular. J12 runs ADM-07 approval (step 8), then ADM-14 token deploy and configure under owner quorum (step 9), then ADM-28 marketing approval (step 10), then ADM-08 'Goes live' by CAPM with G11 and G13, on-chain and off-chain (step 11, scheduled->live). The spec does it the other way: the go-live precheck requires the token to already be in SM-06 'configured', while listing.go_live also carries custody vault V1 'for the token's compliance configuration'. Either the configuration happened under some other approval, which makes V1 on this request meaningless, or the precheck can never pass. The spec also makes scheduled->live an automatic sweep with no G13 act. The token state and rules hash come from A27/A24, and neither is in A36's dependency closure.
findings.fix: Follow J12. listing.go_live (4E+Q, CAPM -> CCO) moves compliance_review->approved with no custody operation. Token configuration stays under ADM-14's own approval in A27/A28. Guard scheduled->live on a configured token whose rules hash equals A19's expectedOnchainParams, plus a CAPM G13 act at or after opens_at if the product map's ADM-08 row is kept. Otherwise record as a decision that opening at opens_at is automatic. Add A27 as a dependency (it is in AM2, so milestone order is fine), or read the token state through an A19 fact, and move OFR_TOKEN_NOT_CONFIGURED onto the scheduled->live guard.

findings.issue: A43 is a missing dependency for gate G17. Submit and go-live preconditions call 'A43's claims check', and the go-live precheck needs zero open G17 flags. Sponsor tasks ('Respond to RealX review') and notifications to the CAPM queue and to the sponsor also come from A43. A43 is not in A36's dependencies or their transitive closure. The builder therefore has no claims interface and will stub G17, and the G17 planted-failure test can then pass against a fake.
findings.fix: Add A43 to A36's dependencies. Both are AM3 and A43 depends only on A14 and A35, so there is no cycle. In the Specify list, name the A43 interfaces this node calls: the claims check (returning flags with phrase, location and state), the task call and the notification call.

findings.issue: The sponsor declaration is missing, which breaks SPN-06 and D04. SPN-06 in the product map lists a 'Sponsor declaration', and the mock shows it 'Signed 20 Sep'. A03's delegable.ts marks 'the sponsor declaration at submission (SPN-06)' as "counsel", which is treated as non-delegable until counsel answers. A36's document_set and submit preconditions leave the declaration out, and the agent-parity paragraph lets a sponsor agent submit with no carve-out. A build could therefore let an agent submit a listing without a human's passkey-signed declaration, and the pass criterion 'tokens behave as their human for maker actions' would accept it.
findings.fix: Add sponsor_declaration to document_set as an A35 e-signature by SP-OWN or a director, with a passkey step-up. It is human-only while delegable is "counsel", and a token attempt is refused with the non-delegable code. Add OFR_DECLARATION_MISSING as a submit precondition. Add a test that refuses a sponsor token trying to sign the declaration. Log the question under HG-LEGAL.

findings.issue: The seed conflicts with A06 and with A36's own rules, and A36 writes into A06's owned path. (a) A36 seeds Unley Road as 'live at 91 percent' and the challenge expects 'Open offer', but A06 seeds UNL01 as closed on 21 Sep with 9,100 units allocated and the mint pending. A36's own line 67 says A06 resolves design bug 6 that way. (b) A36 requires a second approved 'Coming soon' offering, but A06 has exactly 8 trusts and says 'Coming soon' appears only after APR-2290 passes. (c) Marine Parade is seeded in compliance_review with the insurance certificate 'Missing', but A36's own OFR_DD_INCOMPLETE rule refuses to submit with a missing due-diligence item, so that state cannot be reached through the module's transitions and would have to be inserted directly. (d) 'Integration: the seed' writes into <workspace>\app\packages\db\seed\, which A06 owns, and that breaks the 'only owned paths changed' rule.
findings.fix: Align with A06. UNL01 is closed or finalising, shown publicly as 'Closed', so the public gallery shows 'Open offer' only for KST01 and ANN01; update the challenge and pass criteria to match. Either ask A06 to add the approved future offering, or drop that requirement. For MPA01, make a missing due-diligence item a warning at submit and a blocker at go-live (the same pattern as G17), or seed a lapse after submission. State that A36 only ships fixtures inside its own module path for A06's loader, or only verifies A06's seed.

findings.issue: The retained stake is undefined, which hides a supply question and a holder-cap question. The check 'sponsor_retained_stake_bps + (10,000 − sponsor_retained_stake_bps) accounts for the whole supply' is always true, so testing it proves nothing. The spec never says whether retained units are inside supply_units or on top of it. The hard cap is price × supply_units, and the design sells all 10,000 units (KST01 hard cap = 10,000 × A$238.40), so a 10 percent retained minimum would mean 11,000 units in total. That contradicts A06 ('every trust 10,000 units') and changes what A38 mints. The spec also silently exempts the retained stake from the 5 percent holder cap (G07).
findings.fix: Define offered_units and retained_units explicitly, with supply_units = offered + retained and hard_cap_cents = price × offered_units, and say which one the design numbers use. Reconcile with A06's seed. Replace the always-true check with a real one: offered + retained = supply, and retained = ceil(supply × bps / 10,000). Record the sponsor's G07 exemption as a counsel or founder question stored as a data row.

findings.issue: The oracle flag and the oracle rule disagree. The graph and the frontmatter say oracle: no, but the Oracle rule and pass criterion 1 require 100 percent of the hidden tests in gauntlet\hidden\A36 to pass. If the orchestrator schedules the Oracle stage from the graph flag, that folder is never created, and the criterion either cannot be met or is met by an empty folder.
findings.fix: Set oracle to true for A36 in the graph and the frontmatter; the node fixes the cap arithmetic that bounds escrow and the close triggers. Otherwise, have the App Gauntlet run the Oracle stage for any node whose spec lists hidden cases, and add a check that the hidden folder has at least one case for each of oracle items (a) to (k).

findings.issue: Several challenges and 'done' conditions rely on nodes that come later or are not dependencies, so they cannot be checked at this gate, or a fake can satisfy them. (a) 'An A101 anomaly event': A101 comes after A48, which comes after A36. (b) The same-tick G11 refusal is an order-concurrency property of A37, which is a child node. (c) The MCP catalogue needs A104, which is not in A36's dependency closure. (d) The agent-parity suite is A100, in AM8. In addition, remaining_to_hard_cap_units has no formula: the challenge implies pending plus funded, while the close rules use funded only.
findings.fix: Restate each as something this node owns. (a) Emit the security event that A101 later consumes. (b) Test getOfferFacts against A19's evaluator with synthetic facts, and leave the concurrency race to A37. (c) Add A104 as a dependency, or check the OpenAPI x-realx scope and delegable markers instead. (d) Treat A100 as a later confirmation, not a pass condition here. Define remaining = supply − (funded + pending) for first_come, and ceiling − (funded + pending) for pro_rata.

findings.issue: The client-money delta line duplicates A37 with a different formula. A36 computes escrow_balance_cents − funded_cents by reading A16, which is not in its dependency closure. A37 already owns GET /v1/offerings/{id}/escrow, where the delta is Σ(order total − fee) over funded, allocated-before-release and refund_pending orders, against the offer_escrow balance. The two results diverge after allocation or during refunds, so ADM-08 could show a false break or hide a real one. The spec also never says whether an application's 'Amount' includes the 0.5 percent fee. The design shows A$2,395.92 (fee included) against a raised figure of A$2,384.00 (fee excluded).
findings.fix: Remove A36's own delta. A71 should bind the ADM-08 line to A37's escrow endpoint, and escrow_balance_cents should go unless A16 becomes a dependency and the formula is copied exactly. Define application amount_cents as subtotal plus fee, and raised_cents as the sum of subtotals. Use the five design rows as test vectors.

findings.issue: There are access-control gaps on actions agents can reach. (a) Investors may call simulate on any offering id, which reveals that draft and compliance_review offerings exist and shows their terms, breaking the not-public-until-approved rule (design bug 19). (b) The out-of-limits decide endpoint has no scope and no rule on whether a token may call it, although accepting an out-of-limits term is approval-like. (c) Sponsor offer requests have no scope and no tenant action code, although they need 4E approval on the sponsor side. (d) Pause is SGL+R, done 'with a passkey', but agent parity lists pause as reachable by agents, and an SGL+R action takes effect immediately.
findings.fix: (a) Allow simulate only for the offering's tenant users and for staff with offerings:review; everyone else gets 404 on a non-public offering. (b) Add offerings:limit_decide for CAPM and CCO, human-only, with a test that refuses a token. (c) Map requests to offerings:submit and name tenant action codes such as offer.request.extend in A33's tenant_approval_rule. (d) State whether a staff agent may execute a pause or may only draft it, and add a test for that.

findings.issue: The spec uses parameter and interface names that the upstream nodes do not define. listing.valuation_max_age_days (90) is not an A19 key; A19 has valuation.max_age_days = 183 for G20. sponsor.min_approvers is not in A33, which uses tenant_approval_rule rows for listing.submit. The ADM-07 constraints panel in the product map shows 'wholesale only, s708 disclosure, documents required', but constraints_snapshot has no fields for these.
findings.fix: Put the 90-day submission limit in A36's own offer_limits, marked set_with_counsel, or use A19's key and state 183 days. Use A33's evaluateSponsorApproval and tenant_approval_rule. Add eligibility, disclosure_type and documents_required[] to constraints_snapshot.

findings.issue: The go-live precheck never re-checks the offer dates. opens_at is checked only at submit, but review can take 5 business days or more, with returns. An offer can therefore be approved after its opens_at or even after its closes_at, then run approved->scheduled->live->closed->failed in consecutive ticks and publish a dead offer.
findings.fix: Add a go-live precheck rule: closes_at − max(now, opens_at) must be at least a minimum offer period (a data row), and closes_at − opens_at must not exceed offer_period_days_max. Otherwise refuse with OFR_DATES_STALE. Add the case to oracle item (f).

findings.issue: Minor accuracy issues. 'OfferProgressCard template' is not a name in the design file; lines 581-587 are an unnamed sc-if block. The 'finalise-and-mint node' (A38) is never linked. The WLG01 vector 'validates' even though its 40 percent soft cap is below soft_cap_bps_min. ADM-08's investors count has no field in the raise snapshot. INVM is an ADM-07 role but gets read access only. Design 'submitted by Tom H.' (ADM-07) and APR-2290's maker 'Tom H. (Listings)' look like a RealX staffer, but in the spec a sponsor user submits.
findings.fix: Cite the spOffer block at lines 581-587. Link A38. State that WLG01 returns zero blockers and one out_of_limits item. Add investors_count to raise_snapshot. State INVM's role on ADM-07. Decide who Tom H. is in the seed and name the maker of APR-2290 separately.
